cands.bio: Democratic California Assemblymember since 2014 (District 44, then 42). Former two-term mayor and city councilmember of Thousand Oaks, and former systems engineer at Teledyne and Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Lab. Won the 2026 election for California's 26th Congressional District.

controversies.text: In September 2019, Politico reported that Irwin carried a bill (AB 873) to narrow the state privacy law while her husband was Ring's chief operating officer. She had disclosed his job, and the state ethics agency said it had received no complaints. She said her role is independent of his job.

endorsements.text: 2026: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Environmental Voters and Equality California.

2026 campaign site lists endorsements from U.S. Sens. Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla, Gov. Gavin Newsom, Rep. Julia Brownley, Assembly Speaker Robert Rivas, and Ventura County District Attorney Erik Nasarenko.
2014 Assembly run: Ventura County Deputy Sheriffs Association, California Professional Firefighters, Ventura County Sheriff Geoff Dean and other law-enforcement groups.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from her on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026, so there are no self-reported answers there. We found no pledge by her on refusing foreign-linked or big-donor money. The campaign site page was cut off, so some of its content could not be read. Her 2026 platform appears only as general statements about public safety, affordability and opposing the Trump administration.

qual.why: She has held legislative and local executive office for roughly two decades, with budget and tax-policy experience, which fits the high band for this office.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site says that on the Thousand Oaks City Council she was a strong advocate for preserving open space and for responsible development.

second-amendment.evidence: Authored 2019 legislation that strengthened Gun Violence Restraining Orders (red-flag orders), including allowing them to extend up to five years and requiring law enforcement agencies to have policies on using them.

cands.name: Sam Gallucci

money.note: Individuals gave $239,060; PAC money $6,000; candidate's own money $292,471. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican who ran for U.S. House in California's 26th District in 2026. He placed second in the June 2 top-two primary and lost the November general election to Democrat Jacqui Irwin. He was also a candidate in the 2021 California gubernatorial recall election.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these voter guide recommendations for his 2026 campaign: April's Common Sense Cali Voters (a Sway voting group), Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide (a Sway voting group), and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he moved to California. We could not find his career, education or any office he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2021 or 2026, and we found no campaign-site or interview statements. So we could not document his stated positions or actions on data centers, property taxes, housing and land, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or development.
